**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

**What I checked**

- **§ 5 (Compensation)** — the planner's primary candidate. Client-payable amounts are limited to fees per Exhibits A/B, including minimum monthly floors ("not less than $____ per month"). These are consideration for services actually delivered, not damages, so they fall outside the rule. § 6 makes those minimums non-contestable, which is a payment-mechanics point rather than an LD exposure.
- **§ 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail)** — the second candidate, where a per-message or stipulated-damages charge would have been the likely exposure. It contains only conduct restrictions (news-group and mass-mailing thresholds) with no monetary consequence attached. § 8f likewise reserves only technical mechanisms and "all legal and equitable rights," i.e., ordinary remedies, not a fixed sum.
- **§ 13–14 (Term / Termination)** — no early-termination fee, no minimum-term buyout. Client's wind-down exposure is continued fees through the last day of the month following its notice month, roughly one to two months, comfortably inside the 3-month fallback even if characterized as a termination cost.
- **Text sweeps** — "liquidated damages," "penalt," "damages," "shall pay," and a regex for `$`/"stipulated"/"forfeit"/"minimum" surfaced nothing beyond the § 5 fee provisions.

**Direction analysis:** the rule only bites when the *Customer* pays. Nothing in this Agreement requires Mortgage Logic.com to pay a penalty or stipulated sum, and there is no Vendor-side LD or service-credit regime either (whose absence is a separate SLA question, not this rule). The preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer — is already met on the face of the document, so per the instruction not to redline compliant findings, I made no edit.

**One flag for your broader review, outside this rule:** § 5(a) leaves the minimum monthly fees as blanks (`$____`), and § 6 twice cross-references "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" when the minimums actually sit in Section 4/5 as numbered here — the section numbering in this document runs oddly (§ 6 and §§ 13–16 are grouped under the § 12 heading). Unfilled minimums that are contractually non-contestable could become a real committed-spend exposure once populated, and the mis-citation weakens the carve-out. Worth confirming the figures and correcting the cross-reference, though neither is a liquidated-damages deviation.
